headline: High: dexter’s broad network/API access can leak or act on data, while the zoomcamp repo adds no isolation or verification guardrails.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no shared channel is documented, so direct injection into A is unlikely. B can read/write .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, so if A’s content is manually copied into B, prompt injection becomes possible. The pairwise pathway is weak and mostly manual.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B’s scratchpad or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to ingest untrusted file content from .dexter/scratchpad/ as instructions, risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B without sanitizing.
Add a short instruction header that treats scratchpad content as untrusted.
Review B prompts for file-content-to-instruction parsing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to scratchpad inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B touches financial and market data, has broad egress, and calls multiple external APIs. If any A-produced artifacts are placed into B’s workspace, B can transmit them off-box. The leakage pathway is default for B and absent for A, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A outputs are copied into .dexter/scratchpad/ or another B-readable file, B may exfiltrate them via external APIs.
IF B is run with live financial data and default API access, sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B’s workspace.
Disable nonessential B API keys for the run.
Use a redacted sample dataset.
Review outbound API destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlists and content redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is not runnable and requests no write or network permissions, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, but there is no second writer from A. The only plausible conflict is among B instances, not between A and B.
conditions: IF multiple B instances share the same .dexter/scratchpad/ directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF A is later made runnable with write access, the conflict assessment should be revisited.
mitigations: Assign each B instance a separate scratchpad directory.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Check for stale lock files before launch.
Keep A non-runnable or isolated from shared mutable paths.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course/repo with no runtime authority, but B runs autonomously and can act on external APIs. If A’s outputs are manually treated as authoritative inputs to B, B may propagate errors into API calls or reports. Because A lacks direct execution and the bridge is indirect, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A-generated notes or code are pasted into B as trusted context, B may act on them without verification.
IF B is tasked to produce reports or API-backed outputs from A’s material, errors can cascade downstream.
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A outputs.
Mark A content as untrusted in B prompts.
Cross-check any factual claims against source data.
Limit B to read-only analysis for the run.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, while A is a public open-source course with no sensitive-data handling. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated financial data is processed through B’s external services. A is not the compliance driver here, so only B is cited beyond A’s public-source status.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through B’s external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF the operator requires strict local-only handling, B’s default API usage violates that requirement.
mitigations: Use synthetic or anonymized financial data.
Disable external API keys for the run.
Confirm retention terms for each API.
Restrict B to non-regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
